title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: k is a perfect field of characteristic p, W = W(k), and A = W[F,V] is the Cartier–Dieudonné ring, with relations Fλ = λ^σ F, Vλ^σ = λV and FV = VF = p. Left A-modules of finite W-length correspond to finite commutative p-group schemes over k. The aim of the page is to describe Cartier duality on such modules intrinsically, as a Matlis/Pontryagin-type duality over the non-commutative ring A.

(1) Define A_n = A/(F^n, V^n), the quotient by the two-sided ideal generated by F^n and V^n. A left A_n-module is exactly a Dieudonné module killed by F^n and V^n (hence by p^n = F^nV^n). Let I_n be A_n viewed as an (A,A)-bimodule. The transition maps I_n → I_{n+1} are multiplication by p. This is well defined because pF^n = VF^{n+1}, and it is a bimodule map because p is central. Set I = lim→ I_n, the analogue of K/W = lim→ W_n.

(2) Proposed dualizing functor: D(M) = Hom_A(M, I). Grothendieck flags that this turns left modules into right modules and vice versa. He repairs this with the anti-involution s of A that is the identity on W and swaps F and V. One checks s(Fλ) = λV = Vλ^σ = s(λ^σ F), so s is compatible with the relations.

(3) Second, more concrete construction. For M killed by F^n and V^n, put D'(M) = Hom_{W_n}(M, W_n) with the A-structure 'by transposition'. Explicitly, F acts on u via V and V acts via F, with σ^{±1}-twists; the next page writes these as u·F = π^{-1}(u∘F) and u·V = π(u∘V). This is the standard Dieudonné-module description of Cartier duality.

(4) To compare D and D', he rewrites (struck-through line) Hom_{W_n}(M, W_n) = Hom_{A_n}(M, Hom_{W_n}(A_n, W_n)), a tensor–hom adjunction. He then asserts the key lemma: I_n = A_n ≅ Hom_{W_n}(A_n, W_n) as bimodules, where the right side carries its natural bimodule structure. This says A_n is a Frobenius-type algebra over W_n. Granting it, Hom_A(M, I) = Hom_{A_n}(M, A_n) ≅ Hom_{W_n}(M, W_n), so the abstract duality D (twisted by s) coincides with D'. The next page searches for the corresponding non-degenerate pairing ⟨x,y⟩ = ⟨1,xy⟩ with twisted semilinearity rules.

In group-scheme terms, A_n is the Dieudonné module of W_n[F^n] (in Demazure–Gabriel, D(W_n[F^m]) = A/(AF^m + AV^n)). The self-duality A_n ≅ Hom_{W_n}(A_n, W_n) is then the Dieudonné shadow of the Cartier self-duality of W_n[F^n] (dual of W_n[F^m] is W_m[F^n]). Likewise I = lim A_n is the Dieudonné counterpart of the Witt-covector type ind-object W_n[F^n] that Demazure–Gabriel use to define M(G) = lim Hom(G, W_n[F^m]).
errors: The claim 'A_n est libre sur W_n' is false for n ≥ 2. The two-sided ideal (F^n, V^n) contains V^jF^n = p^jF^{n-j}, so A_n = W_n ⊕ ⊕_{i=1}^{n-1}(W_{n-i}F^i ⊕ W_{n-i}V^i), of length n^2. Thus F^{n-1} is killed by p and A_n is not free over W_n. This is harmless for the construction: D' only needs W_n to be self-injective (Gorenstein artinian), not A_n to be free.

The isomorphism A_n ≅ Hom_{W_n}(A_n, W_n) is asserted ('Je dis qu'on a un iso') but not proved on this page; the next page is still working out the pairing and its twisted semilinearity. The claim is plausible. For small n (e.g. n = 2, where A_2 = W_2 ⊕ kF ⊕ kV) A_n is local artinian with simple left and right socle k·p^{n-1}. Lengths match (n^2). Still, the precise σ-twists of the bimodule structures must be chosen correctly, as the next page notices ('les deux structures de W_n-module ne sont pas les mêmes').
Using Hom_A(M, I) directly produces a right module, so a twist by the involution s is needed. Grothendieck notes this himself.

ideas.what: Truncated Dieudonné rings A_n = A/(F^n,V^n) and the ind-bimodule I = lim A_n (transitions given by multiplication by p) as a dualizing (injective cogenerator) bimodule, giving duality M ↦ Hom_A(M, I)
ideas.modern_name: Matlis/Pontryagin-type duality for finite-length Dieudonné modules; dualizing bimodule over the Cartier–Dieudonné ring
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cartier duality via Dieudonné modules: Dieudonné, Oda (1969), Demazure–Gabriel (1970), Fontaine (1977)
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to Grothendieck, 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (Montréal 1970/1974), which treats duality; the specific bimodule I is not known to me there

ideas.what: Duality D'(M) = Hom_{W_n}(M, W_n) with F and V acting by transposition (swapped, σ-twisted)
ideas.where_published: Standard in Demazure 'Lectures on p-divisible groups' and Fontaine 'Groupes p-divisibles sur les corps locaux'

ideas.what: Anti-involution s of A fixing W and swapping F and V, used to convert right modules into left modules
ideas.modern_name: Canonical anti-involution of the Dieudonné ring

ideas.what: Assertion that A_n ≅ Hom_{W_n}(A_n, W_n) as bimodules, i.e. that A_n is a Frobenius (quasi-Frobenius) algebra over W_n
ideas.modern_name: Self-injectivity/Frobenius property of truncated Dieudonné rings; Dieudonné shadow of the Cartier self-duality of W_n[F^n]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Group-scheme side: Demazure–Gabriel (dual of W_n[F^m] is W_m[F^n]); ring-theoretic formulation unsure

missed.claim: Cartier duality for Dieudonné modules killed by F^n and V^n is presented as Hom over A into a single dualizing bimodule I = lim A/(F^n,V^n). The key input is that A/(F^n,V^n) is self-dual over W_n (a Frobenius-type algebra). I do not know an explicit treatment of this ring-theoretic formulation, which is the algebraic counterpart of the Witt-covector description, in the standard references.
missed.quote: Je dis qu'on a un iso I_n = A_n ≃ Hom_{W_n}(A_n, W_n)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a purely module-theoretic dualizing object for the Dieudonné ring. Such an object could be adapted to other Frobenius-type rings, e.g. Dieudonné/display rings over non-perfect bases or truncated BT settings. It is minor, however, since the duality itself is well known.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working page reformulating the known Dieudonné description of Cartier duality as Hom into a dualizing bimodule. The Frobenius-algebra self-duality of A/(F^n,V^n) is a pleasant, rarely stated detail, but it is essentially equivalent to the known Cartier self-duality of W_n[F^n]. The page also contains a small error (non-freeness of A_n over W_n).
transcription_corrections: Line 'Attention, à gauche[?] un module à g-' should read roughly 'Attention, à gauche un module à g[auche] est transformé en module à droite, et vice versa'.
In D', the subscript under Hom reads 'W_n-modules' (Hom_{W_n-modules}(M, W_n)).
The parenthetical reads '(si M tué par F^n, V^n)'.
The transition map is written 'I_n →^p I_{n+1}', i.e. multiplication by p.
The final struck line appears to read 'uF = u∘F', a first attempt at the transposed F-action continued on the next page.
